title: FedAPEN: Personalized Cross-silo Federated Learning with Adaptability to Statistical Heterogeneity

problem.claim: Cross-silo federated learning must address statistically heterogeneous client data, which lowers accuracy; clients may also hold architecturally different private models.

gap.claim: Existing personalized federated learning approaches are suited only to particular heterogeneity levels, while real-world heterogeneity is often immeasurable, making approach selection difficult.

contributions.claim: FedAPEN combines mutual learning and ensemble learning to leverage private and shared global models while allowing heterogeneous model architectures.
FedAPEN introduces two mechanisms to coordinate and promote model ensemble without prior knowledge of data heterogeneity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present FedAPEN as a novel federated learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world datasets covering label-distribution skew and feature-distribution skew.
The authors report that FedAPEN almost achieves superior accuracy across varying types and degrees of heterogeneity compared with baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Statistical heterogeneity among cross-silo clients reduces federated learning accuracy.
Existing personalized approaches depend on specific heterogeneity levels, which are often immeasurable in practice; organizations may also use architecturally different private models.
FedAPEN combines mutual learning and ensemble learning and adds two coordination mechanisms for adaptable model ensemble without prior heterogeneity knowledge.
Experiments cover four real-world datasets and multiple label- and feature-distribution skews.
The authors report nearly superior accuracy against baselines across varying heterogeneity types and degrees.

source_observation.claim: A framework combines mutual learning and ensemble learning to use both private and shared models while supporting heterogeneous architectures.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary model-sharing strategies may improve personalization when clients differ in both data distributions and model architectures.

application.claim: Consider coordinated private-global model ensembles for federated settings with unknown statistical heterogeneity and heterogeneous client models.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is effective beyond the reported datasets, skew types, or architectural settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two proposed mechanisms.
Quantitative accuracy results, baseline identities, and statistical significance are not reported.
The abstract does not describe the degree or form of architectural heterogeneity evaluated.
